paragraphs: Hi, I’m Haley, a free spirit, a lifelong learner, and someone who believes the best lessons often happen outside the classroom. Since 16, I’ve been taking solo trips across Southeast Asia, hitchhiking along unfamiliar roads and sleeping on the couches of strangers who became friends. Along the way, I grew endlessly curious about people and cultures: how they live, what they value, and what connects us. That curiosity shaped my university years, where I studied marketing and business while spending much of my time on community projects.

That curiosity followed me into my uni years where I studied Marketing Management but also spent just as much time outside lectures to do projects. I was project manager for a non-profit bringing liberal arts education to Vietnamese students, founded by Stanford's alumni. In a system where learning often means chasing grades and achievements, many Viet students rarely get the chance to ask “why,” to question, debate, and think independently. In my role, I reached out to sponsors and partners to fund our programs, built collaborations with 20+ organizations including the U.S. Embassy in Hanoi, and led the campaign that brought our Summer Program young students nationwide. With the time joining TEDx community in Hanoi, I also organized events for youth, partnered and called for sponsorships from enterprises.

Stepping into the private sector, I grew fascinated by technology and products, and by how a good product can solve real problems.  At Zalopay, one of Vietnam’s leading fintech companies, I work on growth and own a UGC program. Beyond being a payment platform, Zalopay helps millions of Vietnamese people manage their everyday finances, save, and invest so their money can grow toward the plans and dreams they hold for the future. Optimizing product and communicating to millions of users every day has taught me lessons about understanding users and it has shown me firsthand how technology can make everyday life simpler, safer, and fairer.

Education and technology are still where my heart is. Over the years, I’ve learned that good intentions need both heart and evidence to create real change. On the communication side, I know how to plan a campaign from the first brief, craft stories that resonate with different audiences, and build partnerships that bring the right people to the table. On the data side, I work with numbers every day to track user behavior and use data for decision-making. I’ve seen how a single insight from the numbers can reshape an entire campaign, and how a well-told story can make those numbers matter to people.

That combination is what I hope to bring to the causes I care about. Many NGOs and community projects are doing incredible work but struggle to reach the people who need them most, or to show the impact they’re already making. I’d love to help close that gap: by amplifying voices that deserve to be heard, measuring what truly matters, and turning good ideas into movements that last.
Alongside my full-time role, I’m actively looking for side projects with NGOs, educators, and mission-driven teams, especially in education, youth development, and tech for good.
The Best Projects start with a Conversation. Let’s have one!
